clue.text: Poetess who reaches an Indian station by train from a distant station, after writing about plants

definitions.text: Poetess who reaches an Indian station by train

indicators.note: the station's name is set after the plant writing, so it comes second in the answer

parts.note: a flora is a written catalogue or treatise describing the plants of a region
Crewe is a major railway junction in Cheshire, England, far from India

explanation.surface: A poet travels by train across India after a career of botanical writing.
explanation.walkthrough: The poetess is the heroine of Tom Stoppard's play Indian Ink, who travels by train to an Indian hill station; CREWE is a famous English railway junction.
explanation.definitionFit: Stoppard's Indian Ink centres on a fictional English poet who journeys by rail to Jummapur in 1930.

clue.text: Ancient goddess, something unlikely to be seen this summer, we hear

indicators.note: says the clue's description is to be taken as heard, a word pronounced the same

parts.words: something unlikely to be seen this summer
parts.note: a village fete, an outdoor summer fair, likely cancelled in a pandemic summer

explanation.surface: A remark that an old goddess is as rare this summer as an outdoor celebration.
explanation.walkthrough: A FETE is a British outdoor fundraising fair, typically held in summer; this one was written in a year when such events were cancelled.
explanation.definitionFit: Each of the three Fates of Greek myth was a goddess spinning and cutting the thread of life.

clue.text: Slow learning is the characteristic method adopted by some Germans

indicators.note: the method is taken in by the Germans, so it sits inside their name

parts.note: Ossis is the colloquial name for former East Germans
MO, modus operandi, is someone's characteristic way of working

explanation.surface: Gradual absorption of knowledge is a typical approach of certain Germans.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Adopted by' puts the method inside the Germans; Ossi is German slang for someone from the former East Germany, used after reunification.
explanation.definitionFit: Learning by osmosis means picking knowledge up gradually and unconsciously, as fluid seeps through a membrane.

clue.text: Dickensian character using craft to channel rum criminally

parts.note: art and craft both mean skill

indicators.note: the letters of the two words are treated wrongly, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Smuggling liquor through a waterway using some cunning trick.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Craft' reads as a boat beside 'channel', but here it means skill; 'criminally' is the anagram signal for the next two words.
explanation.definitionFit: He is the hero of Charles Dickens's novel Little Dorrit.

clue.text: Baroque royal den that's seen in a play about a prince

definitions.text: that's seen in a play about a prince

indicators.note: baroque means extravagantly ornate or bizarre, so the letters are reshaped

explanation.surface: An ornate royal chamber appears on stage in a drama about a prince.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Baroque' rearranges ROYAL DEN. The play is Hamlet, Prince of Denmark, where this is Polonius's servant sent to spy on Laertes.
explanation.definitionFit: Polonius's servant in Shakespeare's Hamlet is a minor character who appears in Act 2.

clue.text: One wearing a cape is a very slender type

indicators.note: the cape is worn round the one, so it encloses it

parts.note: Cape Wrath is the north-western tip of mainland Scotland
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone in a cloak is described as exceptionally thin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wearing' puts I inside WRATH; the cape is Cape Wrath in Scotland, not a garment.
explanation.definitionFit: Besides a ghost, the word can describe an extremely thin, pale person.

clue.text: Set off for a journey

definitions.meaning: to set off an alarm or switch is to activate it

explanation.definitionFit: To trigger a mechanism is to activate it, and a short excursion is also so called.

clue.text: A poet sounding like someone aggressive in America

indicators.note: signals that the poet's name is pronounced like the aggressive figure's

parts.note: Rambo, the violent hero of American action films, stands for any aggressive person

explanation.surface: A poet whose name echoes a belligerent American.
explanation.walkthrough: The French poet's name is pronounced roughly like RAMBO, the Sylvester Stallone action hero.
explanation.definitionFit: Arthur Rimbaud was the nineteenth-century French Symbolist author of A Season in Hell.

clue.text: A character in an Updike novel having lots of sex with a tart, a noble and old lady

definitions.text: A character in an Updike novel having lots of sex

parts.note: a tart is a kind of pie
a thane was an Anglo-Saxon or Scottish nobleman
ma is a familiar word for mother, one's old lady

explanation.surface: A promiscuous fictional character beds a loose woman, an aristocrat and an elderly woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tart' looks like a loose woman, but it is a pastry. The novel is Couples, where this builder has many affairs.
explanation.definitionFit: The adulterous builder at the centre of John Updike's Couples sleeps with several of his neighbours' wives.

clue.text: I'm the boy to charm paranormal healer's assistant

indicators.note: beyond the normal, so the letters are pushed out of their usual order

explanation.surface: A boy boasts of his supernatural charm in a faith healer's employ.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Paranormal' rearranges all fifteen letters of I'M THE BOY TO CHARM.
explanation.definitionFit: In Brian Friel's play Faith Healer, Teddy is the manager; this name belongs to the healer's assistant in the novel the puzzle draws on.

clue.text: Corrupt cop: "Dirt is clue"- it's certainly evidence of a crime

indicators.note: corrupt means spoiled or perverted, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A bent policeman insists his dirt is a clue to a crime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Corrupt' looks like an adjective for the cop, but it rearranges COP DIRT IS CLUE.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin legal term names the body or facts proving a crime was committed.

clue.text: In scripture, Saul's twin brother?

indicators.note: the brother is found inside the run of letters across these words

explanation.surface: A question whether the biblical Saul had a twin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' points to letters within scripturE SAUl's.
explanation.definitionFit: In Genesis Jacob's twin sold his birthright for a bowl of pottage.

clue.text: Period in a big hospital that's the effect of earlier events

indicators.note: the period goes inside the word for big

parts.note: fat means large or big
a term is a period of time, as in a school term
H is the abbreviation for hospital on maps and signs

explanation.surface: A stay in a large hospital that follows earlier happenings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Big hospital' looks like one phrase, but 'big' and 'hospital' give separate pieces with the period inside the first; 'in' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Consequences of a disaster or event are the period that follows it.

clue.text: An old poem about love as something notable for sailors

definitions.meaning: the Middle English lyric beginning 'Lenten ys come with love to toune' is printed under this title
an exceptionally high and low tide after new and full moon, important to navigation

explanation.definitionFit: The medieval lyric celebrates spring and love, and the term also names the large tides mariners must watch for.

clue.text: In the world of letters, it's useful to put information on the internet about poetry

definitions.text: In the world of letters, it's useful

parts.words: to put information on the internet
parts.note: to post is to upload a message online
C stands for circa, Latin for about
an ode is a lyric poem

explanation.surface: A literary figure finds it handy to upload verses online.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The world of letters' suggests literature but means mail: the code helps sort letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Mail sorters rely on the alphanumeric address code to route envelopes.

clue.text: It's hard to bear for Joanna, a religious lady who has issues about Christmas

definitions.text: for Joanna, a religious lady who has issues about Christmas
definitions.meaning: Joanna's surname in Faulkner's Light in August, a pious woman entangled with Joe Christmas

explanation.definitionFit: A heavy load is hard to carry, and in Faulkner's novel the devout Joanna has a fatal affair with Joe Christmas.

clue.text: There's medium approval in these for London

indicators.note: the medium and approval go inside the word these

parts.note: M is the abbreviation for medium, as in clothing sizes
OK signals agreement or approval

explanation.surface: Some modest approval is found in these for the capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' is the container signal. London got the nickname from the coal smoke that once hung over it.
explanation.definitionFit: Londoners and others long called the capital by this nickname, from its smoky air.

clue.text: Artist or singer in play

indicators.note: the word is put into play, moving its letters around

explanation.surface: An artist or a singer performing in a drama.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In play' rearranges SINGER.
explanation.definitionFit: Jean-Auguste-Dominique Ingres was a French Neoclassical painter.

clue.text: A king in the manner of a criminal

parts.note: GR is Georgius Rex, King George
after means in the style of, as in a painting after Rembrandt

explanation.surface: A monarch behaving like a lawbreaker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In the manner of' gives AFTER, the sense used of artworks in someone's style.
explanation.definitionFit: In slang a swindler or someone using illicit gains is so called.

clue.text: Donne's work he'd written on time, with 1000 pages

indicators.note: in an across clue the written words go on, after, the time

parts.note: he'd written out without the apostrophe gives these letters
a ream is 500 sheets, each with two sides, so a thousand pages

explanation.surface: Donne's piece, which he wrote promptly and at great length.
explanation.walkthrough: A ream is 500 sheets of paper, giving 1,000 pages if both sides count.
explanation.definitionFit: John Donne's love poem in the Songs and Sonnets is titled so.

clue.text: Trap seen in identical rejected mystery stories?

indicators.note: turned back, so the whole combination is read backwards
the trap appears inside the word for identical

parts.note: same means identical
a gin is a snare or trap for animals

explanation.surface: Snares feature in repetitive, cast-off detective tales.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Seen in' places the trap inside the word for identical, and 'rejected' turns the result backwards; 'trap' is the old word for a snare, not a mouth.
explanation.definitionFit: Puzzles or riddles are mysteries, and the question mark admits they are not literally stories.

clue.text: "Something tough" includes hard kind of music for some people to perform

definitions.text: kind of music for some people to perform

indicators.note: the tough thing takes in the hard letter

parts.note: coral is a hard, durable marine growth
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A hardy substance includes a hard sort of music for a group.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Includes' puts H inside CORAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Music for a choir is sung by a group of people together.

clue.text: Hideous charges about international peacekeepers — they sound worrying

indicators.note: the rearranged charges go about, around, the peacekeepers
something hideous is twisted out of shape, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: UN peacekeeping forces of the United Nations

explanation.surface: Grotesque accusations against UN forces sound alarming.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hideous' is the anagram signal and 'about' the container. The word is informal British usage, mainly for the noise of gears grinding.
explanation.definitionFit: These are grinding mechanical noises, such as a gearbox makes when something is wrong.

clue.text: "All nature seems at work. Slugs leave their -" (Coleridge)

definitions.text: "All nature seems at work. Slugs leave their -" (Coleridge)

parts.words: All nature seems at work. Slugs leave their -" (Coleridge
parts.note: the missing last word of the opening line of Coleridge's Work Without Hope, a resting place

explanation.definitionFit: Coleridge's line has slugs emerging in early spring from their den or hiding place.

clue.text: Drop back in some English language classes

indicators.note: the word for drop is read backwards

parts.note: to drop is to lose, as a point in a game

explanation.surface: Falling behind in certain English lessons.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Back' reverses LOSE.
explanation.definitionFit: The acronym stands for English for Speakers of Other Languages, courses for learners.

clue.text: Sixties film with a fairly safe prediction — it's about stalking and revenge

definitions.text: Sixties film with a fairly safe prediction — it's about stalking and revenge

parts.words: Sixties film with a fairly safe prediction — it's about stalking and revenge
parts.note: a title that hedges a promise on the next day arriving, attached to a story of pursuit and vengeance

explanation.definitionFit: The title is a conditional phrase about the day after this one, a promise few would bet against.

clue.text: Pound something out of religious literature

definitions.meaning: the American modernist poet Pound's first name
a book of the Old Testament

explanation.definitionFit: The poet behind the Cantos bore this first name, also the title of an Old Testament book.

clue.text: English to wit, doubly embraced by Wells, surprisingly a Nobel prize winner

indicators.note: the doubled letters are taken in among those of Wells, joining one pool of letters
signals that Wells is jumbled in an unexpected way
the to-wit letters are wanted twice over, so they are repeated

parts.note: ie, id est, means that is, to wit

explanation.surface: An Englishman, as it were, hugged twice by Wells is unexpectedly a Nobel laureate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doubly' repeats the to-wit letters; 'embraced by' and 'surprisingly' together mix them into the letters of the surname. The surface points at the writer H. G. Wells, a red herring.
explanation.definitionFit: The Holocaust survivor and author of Night received the Nobel Peace Prize in 1986.
